reproduction.finding: The failure is NOT h2o-specific and is NOT before SSL_new. A versioned trace of the first run shows SSL_new and SSL_accept are reached; SSL_accept returns -1 with SSL_get_error = 1 (SSL_ERROR_SSL). The S17 LD_PRELOAD trace's missing SSL_new was incomplete instrumentation, not the call flow.

standalone_c.shape: PEM private key -> public-only RSA (n,e + RSA_FLAG_EXT_PKEY) whose rsa_sign/rsa_priv_enc live in a custom RSA_METHOD installed on an ENGINE, adopted with RSA_new_method(engine); SSL_CTX_use_certificate_chain_file + SSL_CTX_use_PrivateKey + socketpair + SSL_new/SSL_set_fd/SSL_accept on one side and SSL_connect on the other

divergence_table.authority: 1 (with SSL_ERROR_WANT_READ on the earlier non-blocking calls); engine priv_enc invoked once
divergence_table.candidate_pre_fix: -1, SSL_get_error=1 (SSL_ERROR_SSL); error stack: rsa_ossl_private_encrypt:missing private key (rsa_ossl.c:400), rsa_sign_directly:RSA lib (rsa_sig.c:821), SSL routines::internal error (statem.c:170); engine callbacks never invoked

root_cause.mechanism_1: rsa_new_intern ignored its ENGINE argument (an explicitly documented 'unreachable' reduction), so neverbleed's custom RSA_METHOD was never adopted; RSA_sign/RSA_private_encrypt dispatched to the default table, which has no private key for the public-only object.
root_cause.mechanism_2: Even with the method adopted, int_ctx_new / do_sigver_init / EVP_PKEY_sign / EVP_DigestSignFinal always took the provider path and ignored pkey->foreign. A foreign legacy key was exported to a provider keymgmt, which rebuilds the key from n/e (the custom RSA_METHOD cannot cross the provider boundary), so the provider's rsa_sign_directly again reached rsa_ossl_private_encrypt with no private key.
root_cause.regression_from_own_conversion: yes — both are reductions introduced by this campaign: the ENGINE block was omitted from rsa_new_intern, and the legacy EVP_PKEY_METHOD half was stubbed with 'pmeth is always NULL' assumptions that a real consumer (h2o/neverbleed) falsifies.
root_cause.evidence: engine_adopted changed 0 -> 1 with the first fix; server_accept stayed -1 until the foreign-key legacy routing landed; the direct C probe and the h2o trace reproduce both stages.

src/rsa/object.rs: rsa_new_intern: restore the authority's ENGINE block (ENGINE_init(engine) / ENGINE_get_default_RSA() / ENGINE_get_RSA, RSA_LIB_106/116 failures, functional reference stored in r->engine).
Rsa::destroy_body and RSA_set_method: call ENGINE_finish(r->engine) at the authority's position.
RSA_new_method/RSA_get0_engine docs updated (the 'engine is ignored' claim removed).
src/rsa/mod.rs: Rsa::engine is typed with the real crate::engine::eng_lib::Engine (layout-neutral: still one pointer).
src/evp/pkey_ctx.rs: int_ctx_new: honour pkey->pmeth_engine/pkey->engine and ENGINE_get_pkey_meth_engine; keytype = OBJ_nid2sn(id) only for a non-foreign key; foreign keys take EVP_PKEY_meth_find(id) with no provider fetch; application methods suppress the fetch; the method's init callback runs and a failed init clears pmeth before release.

EVP_PKEY_CTX_new / EVP_PKEY_CTX_new_id: forward the caller's explicit ENGINE instead of discarding it; the constructor's engine argument now takes the functional reference exactly as the authority does.
EVP_PKEY_CTX_free body: pmeth->cleanup at the authority's position and ENGINE_finish(ctx->engine).
EVP_PKEY_CTX_ctrl: the legacy pmeth->ctrl arm (with the keytype test and the -2 command-not-supported raise).
EVP_PKEY_CTX_dup: the legacy pmeth->copy arm (with ENGINE_init for the copy) instead of the unconditional err:.
src/evp/signature.rs: signature_init_legacy: the authority's pmeth sign/verify/verify_recover init switch, the missing-callback 'return 1', the err: reset and the cached-data replay.
EVP_PKEY_sign: the legacy arm (pmeth->sign) with the M_check_autoarg length-query/short-buffer prelude.
src/evp/digest.rs: sigver_legacy: the authority's legacy init (digest-by-name lookup, default digest NID fallback, signctx_init/digestsign/EVP_PKEY_sign_init chain, set_signature_md, EVP_DigestInit_ex, digest_custom flag).
EVP_DigestSignUpdate: the legacy pmeth digest_custom arm, then EVP_DigestUpdate.
EVP_DigestSignFinal: the legacy digest_custom/SIGCTX_CUSTOM/signctx/EVP_PKEY_sign arms, including the copied-context path.
fix.abi: No export added or removed; no #[repr(C)] line changed; pointer-only Rust parameter type changes are ABI-neutral. The Phase-2 ABI courts all pass.

compatibility_divergences_accepted.divergence: EVP_PKEY_sign's M_check_autoarg error raises (EVP_R_INVALID_KEY for a zero-size key, EVP_R_BUFFER_TOO_SMALL for a short buffer) are not raised; the authority's return values are preserved.
compatibility_divergences_accepted.classification: authority macro-defined raise sites are absent from the generated err-site table; the two branches are not reachable in the h2o/neverbleed shape (the TLS caller queries the length first and allocates that size). Recorded as an evidence gap, not a behavior change in the tested path.

compatibility_divergences_accepted.divergence: EVP_PKEY_CTX_dup takes the ENGINE functional reference immediately before pmeth->copy rather than before the allocation.
compatibility_divergences_accepted.classification: not observable: no callback or error path runs between the two positions for a successful copy; the failure path releases the reference exactly once.

remaining_gaps.gap: EC_KEY_new_method / ossl_ec_key_new_method_int still ignore the ENGINE argument (the same omission class as the RSA one).
remaining_gaps.impact: an ECDSA neverbleed key would still fail; the h2o fixture uses an RSA certificate, so this subphase did not exercise it.

remaining_gaps.gap: The legacy verify half (EVP_DigestVerifyUpdate/Final and EVP_PKEY_verify legacy arms) remains stubbed.
remaining_gaps.impact: server-side h2o only signs with the engine key; a client-side/foreign-key verify path is not claimed.

safety_obligations.notes: All added unsafe operations are dereferences of the context/key/method pointers and calls to the method tables inside private unsafe fns (sigver_legacy, evp_pkey_sign_legacy, digest_sign_final_legacy, signature_init_legacy, int_ctx_new, EVP_PKEY_CTX_dup, ctrl). Each has a SAFETY comment and an explicit precondition. No safe fn was given raw work.
retained_obligations: An EVP_PKEY_METHOD installed by an application must outlive any context built from it (authority contract; standard tables are statics).
ENGINE_init's functional reference is released exactly once: RSA_free/RSA_set_method for Rsa, EVP_PKEY_CTX_free for EvpPkeyCtx, and the dup failure path for its copy.
The method's init must have run before its ctrl/sign/cleanup callbacks; int_ctx_new now calls it and clears pmeth on failure so cleanup never sees a half-built method context.
safety_obligations.hidden_obligations_found: The 'engine is unreachable' claim in src/rsa/object.rs was a hidden false assumption: a real consumer builds an ENGINE and passes it to RSA_new_method. It is removed and the code now honours the argument.

unsafe_block_lines_before_after.metric_note: counted as lines containing 'unsafe {' (grep -c), which includes doc-comment examples and test code; the diff adds call-site unsafe blocks, not new unsafe abstractions

non_claims: h2o reaching L7-functional does not graduate any mechanism to SAFETY_DISCHARGED: no Miri/ASan/negative-control evidence was produced in this FAST-only subphase.
The two focused tests are API/contract tests; the end-to-end claim rests on the standalone SSL_accept probe and the downstream workload, not on the unit tests alone.
The S17 observation 'no SSL_new/SSL_accept' is corrected: a versioned trace shows both calls; the earlier trace did not capture them.
No full library suite, adversarial probe suite or forensic regeneration was run.
